item.title: China ranks among global leaders in 6G patent applications
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-24
SHANGHAI, Nov. 24 (Xinhua) -- China is among the world's top countries in 6G patent applications and has developed more than 300 key 6G technology assets, according to the 2026 Global 6G Development Conference held in Shanghai on Tuesday. "Our 5G networks have been operating for years, laying a solid foundation for 6G evolution, and this foundation has also benefited from cooperation across the global industry," said Wen Ku, chairman of the China Communications Standards Association. As of the end of August, China had built about 5.19 million 5G base stations. From 3G to 5G, globally unified standards have delivered economies of scale that significantly lowered the cost of communications equipment and connected billions of people to the digital world, and 6G should continue on the path of cooperative development, Wen said. Zhong Zhihong, chief engineer of the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, said 6G technology is now at a critical stage of deepening technological breakthroughs and advancing comprehensive standards development, making it all the more necessary for global industry, academia and research parties to build consensus and cooperate closely. At the conference, the IMT-2030 (6G) promotion group, together with major international organizations, industry alliances and leading Chinese and international enterprises, released the Global 6G Development Philosophy Declaration. The declaration sets out five concepts, including cross-domain integrated innovation with intrinsic intelligence at its core, green and sustainable development throughout the entire chain, and a secure and trustworthy system based on all-domain security, among others. The conference also launched a pilot program for 6G innovative development jointly by the ministry and provincial governments. Eight provincial-level regions, namely Beijing, Hebei in north China, Shanghai, Jiangsu, Zhejiang and Anhui in east China, Hubei in central China and Guangdong in south China, are participating to jointly build a coordinated national framework for 6G innovation. ■

item.title: Centuries-old classics show new vibrancy at China's inaugural heritage industries expo
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-24
HANGZHOU, Nov. 24 (Xinhua) -- In simple words, guests and visitors to China's inaugural heritage industries expo in Hangzhou, capital of east China's Zhejiang Province, summed up their impressions as "familiar yet surprised." From celadon jewelry and latte-art tea to silk designed with AI, China's heritage industries have found a second wind, and the first Historical Classic Industries Expo, which was held from Friday to Sunday, is where the applause was landing. Covering an exhibition area of about 30,000 square meters, the event drew more than 400 key enterprises and renowned brands. It highlighted innovation strategies across historical classic industries, including silk, tea, porcelain, and traditional Chinese medicine, all deeply rooted in Chinese culture and traditions dating back centuries or even millennia. A large electronic jacquard loom, which can simultaneously control 42,000 warp threads at high density while significantly reducing labor costs, became an attention-grabber at the expo. Automation and intelligent technologies are empowering a growing number of heritage industries. With AI design models, designers can quickly optimize silk and other product designs based on a massive pattern database and graphic algorithms, greatly shortening the design cycle, said Li Jianhua, chairperson of Hangzhou Wensli Silk Culture Co., Ltd. He noted that Wensli Group's eco-friendly printing and dyeing equipment compresses more than a dozen traditional processes and a production line that once spanned about 5,000 square meters into a single machine of roughly 50 square meters, with virtually zero wastewater discharge. At the exhibition area featuring the industries from east China's Jiangxi Province, staff demonstrated an intelligent capsule tea-and-coffee machine blending delicate latte art with traditional tea, drawing crowds eager for a taste. "Historical classic industries must keep innovating based on tradition and develop products that better meet modern consumer needs," said Fu Zukang, an inheritor of yellow rice wine brewing techniques and Party chief of Kuaijishan Shaoxing Rice Wine Co., Ltd. Fu added that modern equipment can now reproduce traditional brewing in a way better suited to health-conscious consumers, and that the sparkling yellow rice wine the company launched last year has been well received by younger consumers. Guo Jian, director of the celadon and sword industries bureau of Longquan City in Zhejiang, shared a similar view, saying the city's heritage industries are "opening their arms" to modern life, shifting from "doing nothing but waiting for customers" to conducting demand-driven research and development. According to the customs authorities in Lishui, which administers the city, Longquan sword-related exports reached 56.16 million yuan (about 8.37 million U.S. dollars) in the first nine months of this year, up 44.7 percent year on year. Rather than high-end collectible swords, anime and gaming props priced in the tens or hundreds of dollars are proving particularly popular among young people. At the expo's interactive area, Nusrat Jahan Nipa, head of the Bangladesh Heritage Research and Professional Institute, made a creative silk umbrella for her friends back home. Describing herself as a Chinese traditional art enthusiast, she said the innovative hands-on experience on site was very novel and interesting. China unveiled its first national policy document for centuries-old industries this year, as part of broader efforts to leverage the country's rich cultural heritage and build strong global brands. By 2028, the country aims to cultivate 50 enterprises with annual revenues exceeding 10 billion yuan each, according to the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology. The document also calls for 100 Chinese consumer brands and several industrial clusters with annual output exceeding 100 billion yuan to be developed by 2028. ■

During the 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Week in Shenzhen, seven AlphaBot robots stationed at the media center provided services for Chinese and foreign journalists, operating reliably and serving drinks over seven consecutive days. These robots are from Ai² Robotics, a robotics startup founded in early 2023 in Shenzhen by Guo Yandong. Guo believes that humanoid robots must be deployed in real scenarios for practical assignments. With this end goal in mind, he has oriented Ai² Robotics toward developing productivity-focused intelligent robots. The AlphaBot robots are now in service across Shenzhen for airport, industrial, urban governance and emergency-response tasks. item.title: China unveils Shenzhou-24 crew for space station mission, including first foreign astronaut
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-24
* Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo, Wu Yi, and Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali will carry out the Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceflight mission, with Tang serving as commander. * This mission marks the first joint flight of Chinese and foreign astronauts in the history of China's manned space program. * A total of more than 90 scientific experiments and technology tests are planned for the Shenzhou-24 mission. These experiments and tests will cover space life sciences, space material science, microgravity fluid physics and combustion science, fundamental physics, space medicine and new space technologies. JIUQUAN, Nov. 24 (Xinhua) -- Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo, Wu Yi, and Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali will carry out the Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceflight mission, with Tang serving as commander, the China Manned Space Agency announced on Tuesday. China's Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceship is scheduled to be launched at 8:18 a.m. (Beijing Time) Wednesday from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China, Zhang Jingbo, spokesperson of the agency, said at a press conference. The three astronauts are a spacecraft pilot, a flight engineer and a payload specialist, respectively. Tang has participated in the Shenzhou-12 and Shenzhou-17 crewed flight missions and is about to become the first astronaut to visit China's Tiangong space station three times. Wu comes from the country's third batch of astronauts and will embark on his first spaceflight mission. Ali will become the first foreign astronaut to visit Tiangong. Tang later described himself at a media briefing as a witness to two historic moments -- the first Chinese crew's entry into China's own space station, Tiangong, and the upcoming first foreign astronaut's visit to the station. "Five years ago, when we first opened the door of the space station, that excitement is something I still cannot forget," Tang said. He added that, no matter how many times he flies, he will prepare with the mindset of a first-time flyer to ensure complete success. Referring to his Pakistani crewmate, Tang said: "Although we come from different countries, our dreams of looking up at the stars are connected." "Space belongs to all humanity, and exploring the universe is our shared dream." Tang expressed hope for more opportunities to work alongside international colleagues, contributing Chinese wisdom and strength to the peaceful use of space and a community with a shared future for mankind. Wu said that an astronaut has only two states: flying and preparing to fly. "Being selected is not the finish line of a dream, but the starting point of a mission," he said. Wu said the crew made comprehensive preparations in theory, skills, physiology and psychology, and trained emergency responses into muscle memory. "Today I am fully ready. The stars are not far away, and my dream is in place." Ali quoted ancient Chinese poems to express his feelings about his upcoming spaceflight. He called the joint flight a "historic collaboration" and said what comes after the flight matters more than the flight itself. "This mission is not a finish line; it is a launchpad," Ali said. Ali expressed his hope that the next chapter of China-Pakistan space cooperation would grow from one astronaut and one flight to multiple joint flights to the moon, Mars and beyond. JOINT FLIGHT In orbit, Ali will join in the crew's routine work and focus on joint China-Pakistan space science experiments, primarily installing experiment samples and units, and carrying out in-orbit experiments as scheduled, Zhang said at the press conference. Four China-Pakistan cooperative projects in the fields of biotechnology and materials will be conducted during the Shenzhou-24 mission, and Ali will conduct an in-orbit experiment on photosynthetic cyanobacteria, the spokesperson noted. Pakistan is China's all-weather strategic cooperative partner. This mission marks the first joint flight of Chinese and foreign astronauts in the history of China's manned space program. Zhang described it as a landmark achievement in bilateral cooperation as the two countries mark the 75th anniversary of diplomatic relations, and an important manifestation of their traditional friendship. China's space station program offers abundant scientific application resources, stable in-orbit operation capabilities, a mature Earth-space transportation system, and a complete astronaut selection and training system, Zhang said, adding that China looks forward to working with more countries and regions to explore the vast universe, peacefully utilize outer space, and enhance the common well-being of humanity. Ali said China and Pakistan had turned a pilot into an astronaut in a remarkably short span of time. "Now it is time to show this great achievement in orbit and send the world a message that we work hand in hand for the peaceful utilization of space," he said. After a short-term joint flight, Ali will return to Earth together with two Shenzhou-23 astronauts, Zhang Zhiyuan and Li Jiaying, aboard the Shenzhou-23 spacecraft. IN-ORBIT TASKS The Shenzhou-24 mission's main objectives are to complete an in-orbit crew rotation with the Shenzhou-23 crew, maintain routine station operations, conduct space science and application work, and carry out maintenance, public outreach and payload tests, Zhang said at the press conference. A total of more than 90 scientific experiments and technology tests are planned for the Shenzhou-24 mission. These experiments and tests will cover space life sciences, space material science, microgravity fluid physics and combustion science, fundamental physics, space medicine and new space technologies, the spokesperson noted. In space life sciences, researchers will build vascular chips and multi-type organ chips to explore how the space environment affects major physiological processes such as vascular aging, aiming to develop new strategies for preventing and treating age-related vascular diseases. In the field of fundamental physics, the mission will explore new states of matter and new physical laws through optical-lattice quantum simulation and research on novel quantum states, as well as key technologies for inertial measurement based on the space cold-atom interferometer. In space medicine, under the space human research program, the crew will advance multi-omics research and behavioral and brain-function studies in space, and further verify new health-maintenance technologies for astronauts and the public. In aerospace technology, meanwhile, the mission will carry out key tests on a chem-electric hybrid propulsion system using new ionic liquid propellants, as part of efforts to develop new spacecraft propulsion technologies. "China will continue to use the space station as a national space laboratory to steadily advance space science, space applications and space technology, better serving sci-tech progress and economic and social development," Zhang said. (Video reporters: Li Guoli, Liu Yi, Da Rihan, Zhang Sheng, Fang Kuan, Wei Ying, Hong Liang and Sha Shiyuan; Video editors: Zheng Xin and Mu Xuyao) ■

item.title: China continues suspending part of control measures on dual-use items export to U.S.
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-24
BEIJING, Nov. 24 (Xinhua) -- China will extend the suspension of part of its export control measures on dual-use items to the United States from Nov. 28, 2026, to Jan. 27, 2027, the Ministry of Commerce said Tuesday. The suspension of the second clause of the Announcement No. 46 of 2024 was first announced in November 2025 and was originally scheduled to run through Nov. 27, 2026. According to the clause, now suspended, the export of dual-use items related to gallium, germanium, antimony and superhard materials to the United States is not to be permitted in principle, while stricter examinations on end-users and end-use purposes are to be conducted regarding exports of the dual-use item of graphite to the United States. ■

item.title: China leads development of 78 international standards on AI
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-24
BEIJING, Nov. 24 (Xinhua) -- China has spearheaded the development of 78 international standards on artificial intelligence (AI), turning its industrial practices and technological innovations into global public goods, according to the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR). Sun Wei, deputy head of the department of standards innovation under the SAMR, told a press conference Tuesday that the body has made active efforts to help improve the international standards system architecture for AI. Working with leading companies and top research institutions, the SAMR has led the development of 29 foundational and common international standards, covering key areas that include data governance, human-computer interaction, security and trustworthiness, Sun said. In addition, the SAMR has coordinated the efforts of 15 technical standards bodies in developing 49 international standards for sector-specific applications, including smart cities and intelligent manufacturing, according to the official. Sectoral application standards act as a key lever to drive the scaled and standardized implementation of AI technologies. In recent years, the SAMR has expanded its efforts to advance international standards in key areas, such as smart manufacturing, smart cities, smart logistics and smart water management, drawing on China's extensive application scenarios and mature industrial practices. Sun said China's systematic efforts to develop application-oriented standards across multiple industries offered technical standards and practical solutions for wider international adoption, supporting AI-empowered real economy development and inclusive, shared digital transformation. The SAMR also revealed that, in response to common risks such as deepfakes and model "poisoning" in generative AI, China has jointly developed with multiple countries a guideline on addressing risks in generative AI. According to the SAMR, this marked the world's first international standards proposal targeting generative AI governance and can provide key support for promoting the formation of a global consensus on risk management. ■

item.title: Xinhua Commentary: Inviting foreign astronaut to Tiangong signals China's space cooperation commitment
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-24
BEIJING, Nov. 24 (Xinhua) -- China announced on Tuesday that Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali will join in the Shenzhou-24 mission as the first foreigner to board China's Tiangong space station, in the latest move showing that China embraces international cooperation in space exploration with open arms. The upcoming mission will be the first joint flight by Chinese and foreign astronauts in the country's history, and Tiangong for the first time will host a foreign visitor. The significance, however, lies in what this cooperation actually involves. The Pakistani astronaut will not simply be a passenger on a short visit. As a payload specialist during the mission, Ali has undergone tough training in China, including lectures on spacecraft and space station knowledge as well as specialized operations, with emphasis on experiment operations and emergency response. For Pakistan, the gains extend well beyond several days in orbit. The mission offers an opportunity to obtain practical experience in human spaceflight, scientific payload operations and astronaut training, all contributing to its future space ambitions. The exploration of the vast universe and peaceful use of outer space are humanity's shared pursuit and bear on the welfare of all peoples. China advocates the peaceful use of outer space, and engages in active international cooperation to share its continuous advances in space science and technology with the world. Through cooperation with the United Nations Office for Outer Space Affairs, China has opened its space station to international experiments. The first round of cooperation selected nine projects involving 23 institutions from 17 countries, with particular attention to opportunities for developing countries. China's Chang'e-6 lunar mission carried scientific payloads from several countries, including Pakistan, France and Italy. Samples that Chang'e-6 collected from the far side of the moon for the first time in human lunar explorations have since been opened to international research institutions. The Tianwen-1 Mars mission involved cooperation with international partners on payload ride-sharing and tracking and control. China has signed more than 200 space cooperation agreements with over 50 countries and international organizations. Yet some Western coverage views the cooperation primarily through a geopolitical lens. Such reading glosses over who truly benefits from it. Genuine cooperation does not merely give partners a seat on a spacecraft; through training foreign astronauts, helping conduct experiments and offering experience, China enables those without crewed-flight infrastructure to build capacity. International cooperation is no substitute for a country's own long-term investment in science and education, but can make that investment more effective. With the vision of building a community with a shared future in the domain of outer space, China stands ready to work with all countries to strengthen exchanges and cooperation, jointly explore the mysteries of the universe, and deliver more benefits to all humanity. ■

item.title: Xi Story: Vision over a century old meets a changing China
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-24
BEIJING, Nov. 24 (Xinhua) -- Dr. Sun Yat-sen once envisioned an ambitious blueprint for China's modernization in a landmark work compiled from his writings finished between 1917 and 1919, featuring plans for an extensive railway and road network as well as world-class ports. "Many of the goals Dr. Sun Yat-sen set forth have been realized, and what we have accomplished has gone far beyond anything he could have imagined," President Xi Jinping said last week at a museum in honor of Sun, one of the nation's revered revolutionary forefathers, in south China's Guangdong Province. This year marks the 160th anniversary of Sun's birth. Upon arrival at the museum located in the city of Zhongshan, Sun's hometown, Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, laid a floral basket before the pioneer's bronze statue and bowed in tribute. Born in 1866, Sun led the Revolution of 1911 more than a century ago to abolish the absolute monarchy that had ruled China for thousands of years. Earlier in November, Xi addressed a gathering held in the Great Hall of the People in Beijing to mark Sun's 160th birth anniversary, hailing Sun as "a great national hero, a great patriot, and a great pioneer of China's democratic revolution." At the gathering, Xi highlighted Sun's lifelong devotion to the country, noting that Sun's call for "revitalizing China" has inspired generation after generation of Chinese, taking on renewed significance with each passing era. The president called for carrying forward Sun's legacy, working together to advance national rejuvenation, and turning into reality the great dream of all Chinese people since the advent of modern times. Xi's visit to the museum, part of an inspection tour in Zhongshan on Nov. 16, offered a glimpse of how Sun's vision of a strong and prosperous China has taken shape today. Sun once envisioned developing the country around three great ports -- in the north, the east and the south. The three powerhouses of China's economy today, the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region, the Yangtze River Delta and the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, echo Sun's original design, Xi noted at the museum. "Dr. Sun's national railway map envisaged 160,000 kilometers," Xi said, noting that China's railway network has since surpassed that figure. By the end of 2025, the country's railway network had spanned 165,000 kilometers in total, including 50,000 kilometers of operational high-speed railway, which accounted for 70 percent of the world's total. "Today, the Chinese economy ranks second in the world. Chinese people have achieved moderate prosperity in all respects, and the Chinese nation has stood up, grown rich and become strong," Xi said. China is also continuing to make new contributions to the development and progress of human society, he added. This transformation Sun once dreamed of is also evident in his hometown and the surrounding area. Before visiting the museum, Xi inspected the Shenzhen-Zhongshan Link, a mega cross-sea passage connecting cities on opposite sides of the Pearl River Estuary. The link cuts travel time between the technology hub of Shenzhen and the manufacturing city of Zhongshan from about two hours to roughly 30 minutes, facilitating integration across the Greater Bay Area. Over the years, Xi has made several inspection tours of the Greater Bay Area. Sun's former residence and the museum exhibition hall in Zhongshan are just a short distance apart. "I have been here before, but this visit has given me new impressions," Xi said. "The great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation has entered an irreversible historical process," Xi said, calling for sustained efforts to advance the great cause. ■

item.title: Xi extends congratulations on Int'l Day of Solidarity with Palestinian People
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-24
BEIJING, Nov. 24 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping extended congratulations to a UN meeting held on Monday to commemorate the International Day of Solidarity with the Palestinian People. In his message, Xi said that the Palestinian question lies at the heart of the Middle East issue, adding that the current tensions in the Middle East should not divert the international community's attention from the Palestinian issue. The key to resolving the Palestinian question is to stay on course toward the two-state solution and promote the resumption of peace talks between Palestine and Israel, Xi said. He stressed that the governance of the West Bank and post-war reconstruction in Gaza should be advanced in accordance with the principle of "Palestinians governing Palestine," and opposed any land-grabbing or rights-infringing actions targeting the Palestinian people. The international community should translate its consensus and commitments in support of Palestine into concrete actions, promote a lasting ceasefire in Gaza and protect the safety of civilians, Xi said. Xi said that justice will prevail and must not be absent. China has always firmly supported the just cause of the Palestinian people to restore their legitimate national rights, he said. China will continue to work with all countries that cherish peace and uphold justice to promote the early realization of a comprehensive, just and lasting solution of the Palestinian question, based on the rule of international law and with a view to addressing both its symptoms and root causes, Xi said. Such efforts will contribute to lasting peace and stability in the Middle East and make positive contributions to world peace, stability, development and prosperity, Xi added. ■
